perf.summary: Convert the data-dependent branch in the search loop to a branchless predicated update to eliminate branch mispredictions on random keys.
perf.currentCost: Each of the ~log2(len) iterations executes an unpredictable conditional branch (ptr[mid] > key). For random/uniform keys this branch mispredicts ~50% of the time; on PC and especially in-order/short-pipeline mobile cores each misprediction costs ~10-20 cycles, dominating the loop body which otherwise is a load + compare + a couple of adds/shifts.
perf.rationale: The classic lower_bound/upper_bound restructured as base+half is the standard branchless form: it removes the only unpredictable branch from the hot loop, turning each iteration into a fixed-latency sequence (load, compare, conditional-move, add, shift) with no speculation penalty. Total cycle count becomes deterministic ~log2(len) iterations regardless of key distribution, which is a net win whenever the original branch is not highly biased.
perf.risk: Semantics must be verified to match exactly: upper_bound returns the count of elements <= key, i.e. first index where ptr[index] > key. The proposed loop must terminate with n==1 then do one final ptr[baseIdx] <= key correction; off-by-one in the final correction or the half/n update would change results. Must also preserve behavior for len==0 (return 0) and for keys outside the array. Reduces instruction-level branch predictability dependence but introduces a loop-carried dependency through baseIdx (cmov result feeds next address) which can slightly lengthen the critical path on wide OoO cores when the branch was actually well-predicted; the win holds for unpredictable keys, the common case for a general search primitive. No signed/overflow change: baseIdx+half stays within [0,len] as before.

perf.rationale: Zero runtime cost either way (unused usings are elided by the compiler), but removing it improves readability/consistency and avoids a misleading signal that System types are in play. Pure hygiene.
